account: Today I have been following my appointment book: office business, a market walk, lunch at home, town accounts, and now three o'clock tea with my neighbour at the east-bank dock cottage. I have just greeted the neighbour and asked about local affairs; I have not yet heard a reply. The secretary confirmed this visit and said the neighbour had nothing urgent to report. The most noticeable repeated news is that townspeople saw the baker carrying a sack of bread at the inn and near the plaza. I also saw the baker stock the market stall, and the baker told me thirty-two fresh loaves were available at one emerald each. This may simply be normal bread deliveries and sales; I have no evidence of an unusual gathering or another purpose. The baker asked whether upcoming town gatherings would require extra loaves, but none has been confirmed to me. During the accounts appointment, the secretary had no ledgers or bills and asked where the accounts were kept. I checked the treasury: it held 128 emeralds and no ledgers, and I left the funds untouched. I asked the secretary to locate existing supporting records. That is an administrative gap, not evidence of missing money. My next scheduled office appointment is at 16:30, followed by home at 19:00.
